posts.content:
🚨 Ruby fixes three regex engine bugs linked to remote code execution risks

Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine.
⠀
The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution.

Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues:

• CVE-2026-89078
• CVE-2026-93577
• CVE-2026-97229
• CVE-2026-110264
⠀
Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation.

Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

CVE-2026-97229.description: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.

CVE-2026-115863.description: ConnMan through 2.0 has a stack-based buffer overflow via a DHCPv6 Reply message. This occurs in get_domains in gdhcp/client.c. It copies a fixed NS_MAXDNAME (1025) bytes from a DHCPv6 DOMAIN_LIST (option 24) value into a 1026-byte stack buffer dns_name regardless of the actual option length, then walks DNS labels with an unbounded "c += jump + 1" loop. A crafted DHCPv6 REPLY with a DOMAIN_LIST option of >= 1025 non-zero bytes makes the label walk leave the buffer and read/write '.' past its end in attacker-chosen strides. An on-link attacker can trigger this without authentication via a forged Router Advertisement (O=1) and a forged DHCPv6 REPLY matching xid/CLIENTID with a long DOMAIN_LIST. The impact is unauthenticated on-link crash of connmand (runs as root). This was introduced in bb06c47.

CVE-2026-115419 - Unintended disclosure of data element to wrong session in Strands Agents SDK A2A Server

Bulletin ID: 2026-146-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/22/2026 13:00 PM PDT
Description:
Strands Agents is an open-source SDK, available for Python and TypeScript, for building AI ...

https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/rss/2026-146-aws/

#aws #security

CVE-2026-115419.description:
**Summary**  
Strands Agents SDK is an open-source SDK, available for Python (strands-agents) and TypeScript (@strands-agents/sdk), for building and running AI agents. An issue exists where, under certain circumstances, the Agent2Agent (A2A) server shares conversation history across callers with different context\_id values, allowing one caller to read and influence another caller's session.  
  
**Impact**  
The A2A server did not properly isolate conversation state between callers. In multi-tenant deployments, an authenticated remote user could access another caller's conversation history or influence model behavior for other callers (CWE-488: Unintended Disclosure of Data Element to Wrong Session). This affects any deployment where an A2A server is reachable by more than one user or tenant.  
  
**Impacted versions:**  
strands-agents (Python): all versions containing the multiagent.a2a module, < 1.43.0  
@strands-agents/sdk (TypeScript): < 1.5.0  
  
**Patches**  
This issue has been addressed in strands-agents version 1.43.0 and @strands-agents/sdk version 1.5.0. The A2A server now uses an agent factory so conversation state is isolated per A2A context\_id. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.  
  
**Workarounds**  
There is no workaround that fully addresses this issue in affected versions. Until you upgrade, do not expose an A2A server to more than one user or tenant. If multiple callers need access, run a separate A2A server instance for each user or tenant.  
  
**References**  
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, we ask that you contact AWS Security via our [vulnerability reporting page](https://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting) or directly via email to [aws-security@amazon.com](mailto:aws-security@amazon.com). Please do not create a public GitHub issue.

CVE-2026-46652.description: The Goobi viewer is a web application that allows digitised material to be displayed in a web browser. From version 24.03 to before version 26.05, ExternalFilesDownloader.getFilename() extracts the destination filename from a server-supplied Content-Disposition response header and passes it directly to Path.resolve() without stripping directory components. This allows for a malicious HTTP server that the viewer fetches from to supply an absolute path or ../ traversal sequences as the filename, writing attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary path writable by the Tomcat process. When targeting the deployed web-application directory, this yields remote code execution as the tomcat OS user. This issue has been patched in version 26.05.

The passwordless sudo policy permits arbitrary arguments to zmunbound, whose wrapper forwards them to Unbound without restricting the configuration path. An attacker can supply a configuration that retains root privileges and disables the chroot. CVE-2026-93639.description: A missing authorization vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) allows a delegated administrator with no explicit administrative grants to overwrite global Zimlet configuration through ConfigureZimletRequest. The uploaded configuration can also add an attacker-controlled domain to the proxy allowlist of the default class of service. If a signed-in user in that class opens a crafted /service/proxy URL, Zimbra serves attacker-controlled HTML under its own origin. The resulting JavaScript can read mailbox data and perform authenticated actions as the victim. Exploitation requires a delegated-administrator account and access to the admin SOAP service; the browser compromise additionally requires the victim to open the crafted URL. ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.20 are affected.

posts.content:
"Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.

The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.

Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.

This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.

“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.

By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.

The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.

Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.

Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.

Users should update their Signal applications as soon as possible. Otherwise, they should check the call indicator to make sure the call indeed ended."
https://www.securityweek.com/signal-vulnerability-lets-malicious-callers-block-hang-ups/

CVE-2026-15176.description:
A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a location is configured that uses the alias directive together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing the $request_filename variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved when the $request_filename variable is used in an access log format directive. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-97205.description:
NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_core_module module. When asynchronous file I/O (AIO) is enabled in certain configurations, processing a Server Side Includes (SSI) page containing “include virtual” commands may trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) in the NGINX worker process. This may cause memory corruption or a worker process crash. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system, corrupt its memory, or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.
